column1: # Registry of RETRACTED FIGURES — consumed by scripts/doc_gates.sh (GATE 3b).
# WHY THIS IS A SEPARATE REGISTRY FROM RETRACTED_PHRASES.tsv
#   GATE 3 catches a retracted PHRASE. GATE 1 compares integers of >=12 digits. Neither can
#   see a retracted STATISTIC — "1.4σ", "~5,500×", "≈10×" — which is why the surviving
#   "1.4σ above" in reports/evidence/r11/PHASE2_README.md needed a human reading (TR-2 v1.23)
#   and why TR-9's draft-stage note kept "C2 net +1.6" through five revisions (TR-9 v1.20).
#   Both were found by a one-off manual sweep. This file makes that sweep permanent.
# THE EXEMPTION PROBLEM, STATED IN ADVANCE (it is the whole design constraint)
#   A retracted figure is quoted MORE often after its retraction than before: every revision
#   row, every corrections-ledger entry and every "this sentence read X until <date>" note
#   must repeat it in order to record what changed. A naive registry fires on the fix itself.
#   GATE 3 exempts by FILENAME and additionally lets a changelog row narrate the old wording;
#   neither is enough here — the legitimate quotations are in BODY PARAGRAPHS of the same
#   files that also carry live prose, and (measured 2026-08-02) a blanket changelog exemption
#   would have hidden the live defect this gate found on its first run, TR-2 v1.12's "2.0σ",
#   which sat inside a revision row.
#   So GATE 3b has NO automatic exemption of any kind. Every legitimate occurrence is an
#   explicit, content-anchored row in documentation/DOC_GATE_FIGURE_ALLOWLIST.txt, in the
#   shape GATE 4b uses. Anything not allowlisted is a [FAIL].
# FORMAT (tab-separated, 2 columns):
#   <retracted figure, as a FIXED string>
column2: <what superseded it, and where that is recorded>

column1: # BEFORE CHOOSING ONE, RUN THE CENSUS RULE. It is written once, in the header of
# documentation/RETRACTED_PHRASES.tsv ("THE CENSUS RULE", 2026-09-02): six spellings a census
# must grep beyond the registered wording, and five tests for when no single needle can cover a
# claim. It applies to figures unchanged — A1 (the abbreviated value) was found ON a figure.
# CHOOSING THE STRING. Make it as narrow as the corpus allows and no narrower. "+1.6" alone
# matches the most places, including live ledger cells; "net +1.6" matches strictly fewer, all
# of them narrations; "C2 net +1.6" matches fewest and MISSES TR-11 v1.14's `C2 "net +1.6"`,
# where a quote mark falls inside the span. The registry holds the middle form.
# NO LIVE MATCH COUNT IS STATED, AND THAT IS A CORRECTION (round 12 drain-3, item `R11`). The
# two superseded ones are quoted in this sentence in order to name what drifted, so the
# paragraph does contain digits and is not claiming otherwise: it shipped "matches twelve
# places" and "matches six", and both had risen with the corpus while the narrowest form stayed
# put — the numbers were wrong and the conclusion they support was not. What is load-bearing is
# the strict ORDERING, which is a property of the substrings themselves and cannot drift.
# Re-derive any of them with
#   git grep -oF -- '<form>' -- '*.md' | wc -l
# Emphasis markers are not
# normalised away, so a figure that is sometimes bolded mid-span ("1.4σ **above**") must be
# registered on the part that is never marked up ("1.4σ").
# ADD A ROW EVERY TIME A PUBLISHED NUMBER IS RESTATED, not only when a claim is withdrawn.
# WHAT GATE 3b CANNOT SEE — stated here rather than left to be rediscovered, because a gate's
# green banner is read as coverage and these are the places it is not:
#   1. IT DISCOVERS NOTHING. The registry is hand-seeded. A figure retracted and never
#      registered is invisible, and the gate cannot tell an empty registry from a clean corpus.
#      The first nine rows were seeded by walking every `| vN.N |` revision row in reports/ for
#      a quoted numeral and reading each one; that pass is repeatable but it is not automatic.
#      UNDER-SEEDING CONFIRMED 2026-08-02 (item A7). A sweep of BODY prose — supersession verbs
#      and `old → new` numeric arrows outside revision rows, across reports/ and documentation/
#      — found two figures the revision-row pass had missed, and they are now rows 10 and 11:
#        `marginal 21.2` — restated to 21.3 in DESCRIPTION_LENGTH.md's own correction note. Its
#           SENTENCE-SIBLING `marginal 4.6` was already registered and this was not, which is
#           what a value-by-value seeding of revision rows looks like from the outside.
#        `palnbr 16`     — restated to 13 by TR-10 v1.2's Mawangdui erratum.
#      Both fired GATE 3b on registration and are now allowlisted narrations. The body sweep is
#      no more automatic than the revision-row one, so this remains a bound on what has been
#      LOOKED at, never a claim that the corpus is clean.
#   2. FIXED STRINGS ONLY. A re-rounded or re-notated restatement does not match: "2.0σ" is
#      registered, "2σ" and "2.00σ" are not, and "2σ" occurs legitimately in TR-2 as the name of
#      the pre-committed gate — so tightening this one would need the meta-mention machinery
#      before it could be safe.
#      MEASURED 2026-08-02 (round-5 item A6), so the decision is against data rather than
#      against the hypothetical. Seven transformation families were generated for all eleven
#      registered figures and matched as fixed strings across `git ls-files '*.md'`: add or
#      strip a trailing zero; strip the group separator; strip a leading ~ or ≈; σ→sigma;
#      ×→x and ×→times; insert a space before the unit; truncate the decimal.
#        (a) NO ESCAPE EXISTS TODAY. Every variant that is not also a substring of the
#            registered form scores ZERO: 1.40σ, 2.00σ, ~5500×, ~5,500x, ≈10x, ~52x,
#            marginal 4.60, net +1.60, marginal 21.20 — 0 occurrences each.
#        (b) NAIVE WIDENING IS UNUSABLE. The three variants that do hit are the ones that
#            drop a qualifier: "2σ" 16 occurrences, "10×" 37, "52×" 11 — and reading them,
#            the overwhelming majority are unrelated ("52× fewer sub-branches", "10× the
#            price", TR-2's pre-committed 2σ gate). A widening on those three would fire
#            ~60 times to catch nothing.
#      WHAT THAT SWEEP CANNOT SEE, since a clear is weaker than a failure: it enumerates
#      SEVEN hand-chosen families. A restatement that rounds to a different precision
#      (1.4σ → 1.35σ), spells the number in words, or splits it across markup is outside
#      every one of them. The result is "no escape in these families", not "no escape".
#   3. THE ANCHOR IS SAME-LINE. Where a supersession clause is in the same paragraph but on the
#      next line (TR-9's draft-stage note), the allowlist row has to say so in prose.
#   4. LEDGER-COMPLETENESS: HALF-CLOSED 2026-08-02 (item A5). This line used to read "there
#      is no equivalent for this registry; a figure can be registered here and never recorded
#      in the ledger". GATE 11 now runs a FIGURES pass over this file
#      (`scripts/doc_gates.sh ledger-figures`), keyed on RF-<first 8 hex of sha256(figure)>
#      exactly as the phrases pass is keyed on RP-. A figure registered from today on FAILS
#      unless it is either recorded in CORRECTIONS.md or listed, with a reason, in
#      documentation/DOC_GATE_FIGURE_LEDGER_OPEN.txt.
#      WHAT IS STILL OPEN: the adjudication. Four of the eleven are recorded (CX-20, CX-19
#      twice, CX-07; their keys are indexed in CX-21); the other SEVEN have no ledger entry
#      and sit on the open list, printed as [OPEN] with a count on every run. An [OPEN] row
#      is an open defect, not an exemption.
#      WHY THE KEY IS NOT THE FIGURE TEXT, measured: six of the eleven figures OCCUR in
#      CORRECTIONS.md and only four are RECORDED there — "1.4σ" and "≈10×" appear inside
#      CX-19's "How it was found" paragraph as examples of meta-mentions found elsewhere. A
#      text-presence check would have cleared two unrecorded retractions.
#   5. MARKDOWN ONLY — NO LONGER, and the heading is kept so the correction is visible
#      (2026-08-07, gate-blind-spot closure #2): the corpus is `git ls-files '*.md'` PLUS
#      every non-markdown file under reports/evidence/ (54 files, 5.7 MB at extension time).
#      The TRs quote those measurement outputs, and this registry's own motivating "1.4σ"
#      was caught only because it happened to sit in an evidence .md — the same figure one
#      directory over in a .out file was invisible. Measured at extension: exactly one hit,
#      dav_tier1.out's "dav_hist palnbr 16" histogram bin row — a fixed-string collision
#      with the retracted Mawangdui value, not a restatement — allowlisted under the new
#      `literal` class. Figures rendered into images are GATE 6's problem.
#      CORRECTED 2026-08-02 (item A8): this line used to end "…and are ungated entirely for
#      statistics". That is no longer true — GATE 6 now runs a SECOND pass over the tracked
#      figure generators using THIS registry, so a retracted statistic annotated onto a plot
#      fails the gate. What remains true, and is the real residual: GATE 6 greps what
#      PRODUCES the image, never the image, so a figure hand-edited in an SVG editor or
#      committed without its generator is still invisible. Baseline when the pass shipped:
#      9 registered figures x 3 tracked generators = 0 hits.

column2: TR-9 v1.24 (2026-09-02, Codex V2-F11 #1, prose batch P31): the margin §5(f) banked after subtracting a 19.0-bit extended-family charge and a 32.9-bit selection charge from C1's 146.3. WITHDRAWN because a subtraction is a margin only if what is subtracted is a maximum, and 32.9 = log2 C(91,7) is not: the 91 is a ledger of TESTS PERFORMED, while the meta-selection charge is denominated in candidate CONSTRAINT FAMILIES, whose denominator METHODS.md §"The file drawer" records as unpublished and calls a different quantity. It is not maximal on its own denominator either - METHODS.md §"Global observable ledger" recorded 2026-08-30 that entering the omitted H1/H3 family gives 95, and log2 C(95,7) = 33.4 > 32.9. The 32.9 figure itself is NOT retracted; it survives relabelled as conditional. Registered on the four-word margin phrase rather than on "32.9", which is still live and correct.

TR-9 v1.24 (2026-09-02, Codex V2-F11 #3, prose batch P31): the low corner of §4's net-savings envelope, published as 102.7-148.3 bits from v1.22 (2026-08-06). It was built as 127.3 + (-4) + (-20.6), and the -4 is the C2 net endpoint the same batch withdrew (RF-e2b24ea8) as unreachable from any published statement cost. Substituting the supported +0.5 gives 127.3 + 0.5 - 20.6 = 107.2, and 107.2/296.0 = 36.2%, so the published percentage floor moves 35% -> 36%. The high corner 148.3 and the C5-retaining 142.0 are unchanged; the envelope narrows from below only, and no measurement or verdict moves. TR-9 v1.24 (2026-09-02, Codex V2-F11 #3 / V2-F35 #3, prose batch P31): the negative half of C2's published net bracket, "≈ 0 (+2.0 selection-only; -0.6 to -4 under explicit-grammar codings)", carried from v1.7 (2026-07-10). Net is defined at TR-9 §1 as compression minus statement cost. C2's compression is log2 23.325025987... = 4.5438 bits; the declared per-distance-ban family is 6 members, log2 6 = 2.585, giving +1.96 (the published +2.0, correct); the largest statement cost stated anywhere in the corpus is the sensitivity table's 4, giving +0.54. Reaching -0.6 needs a 5.14-bit cost and -4 an 8.54-bit cost, and NO explicit-grammar coding producing either is published or privately recorded (prior_art_check.sh 'C2 grammar statement cost derivation' -> PRIOR_ART=NONE). The mechanical cause was that the bracket's lower endpoint was the maximum COST, sign-flipped. Corrected to +0.5 to +2.0. The verdict does not move: C2 is break-even to marginally explanatory either way. CLOSED 2026-09-02 by prose batch P40 (Codex V2-F35 #3): the two sibling sites in documentation/DESCRIPTION_LENGTH.md - the C2 ledger row and the 2026-07-10 refinement note - now publish +0.5 to +2.0, the sign-is-a-coding-convention inference the note drew from the negative endpoint is withdrawn with them, and both class `open` allowlist rows are deleted. No live site remains.
